_about: THE MASTER of the lab behaviour matrix. BEHAVIOUR-MATRIX.md beside it is generated from this file by `node tools/lab-matrix.mjs --write`, and the gate fails if the two differ: edit here, never there.
tests/lab-browser.test.js runs every row in real Chrome with real input. A state's `setup` builds its board and its `expect` proves the board is what the state claims, before any row acts on it.

A row: `steps` perform the gesture; `intent` says in words what should happen and `expect` says it as checks; `rule` cites the ruling. `standing` is ruled, reading (the proposer's reading, not ruled) or open. `built` is yes (the gate proves it) or todo (the gate proves it still FAILS, and demands promotion the day it passes).

Steps: ["click",x,y] ["move",x,y] ["key",k] ["drag",[x,y],[x,y],[[k,x,y],...]] ["undo"] ["settle"]. Checks: links anchors down (counts); pipes (count, or {hand,link}); linkState {id: up|down|gone}; pins {sel: n}; straight {sel: d}; through {sel: [[x,y],...]}; linksBetween {"a|b": n}; keptAt [[x,y],...]; notice noticeNot (patterns); refused (bool); downStroke (#rrggbb); stroke {id: #rrggbb}; selected [ids]; roles {anchor id: [roles]}, as drawn and as Input judges it. A selector is a link id, or "only" when exactly one link exists.

invariants.I1: The tab holds exactly what the authority holds: the same links, with the same ends and pins, and the same anchors.
invariants.I2: A link is drawn dotted exactly when it is down.
invariants.I3: The canvas draws exactly the links that exist, each along a path.
invariants.I4: No pipe names an anchor that does not exist.
invariants.I5: Nothing is thrown in the page.
invariants.I6: No two links that are up are drawn along the same stretch: a pipe carries one link (2026-09-30).
invariants.I7: An anchor whose transit is off is never a junction, drawn or judged: what arrives there stops, so it is an endpoint (2026-10-02, B277).

routed.about: Two unpinned links routed through one anchor, over pipes laid by hand.

pinned.about: One link pinned at one anchor, with no other way.

pinned, another way.about: One link pinned at one anchor, with another way open below it.

pinned and passed.about: Two links pin the left centre; two only pass the right one.

w-chain.about: A link drawn by hand as a chain of w anchors, S-P1-P2-P3-E.

pins and a g hop.about: A link drawn by hand as S-P1-G-P2-E: two pins with a g anchor between them.

down.about: The routed board with its centre deleted, so both links are down (DEL-01).

blocked.about: Two links want one hand-laid trunk; the older holds it, so the younger is down, blocked by it.

two g paths.about: Anchors S and E placed with w, then two g drags between them: a four-pipe path above and a five-pipe path below. No link.

w path fed by g.about: The director's case: anchors A, B, C; a w path A-P1-P2-B; a g path from C joining P1; links A-B and C-B. A-B has first call on its w pipes, so C-B waits, blocked by it.

two pins beside a g path.about: Anchors S and E, a g path below them through X, and a link S to E pinned at P and Q above, on its own w pipes.

a pin and a g hop beside a g path.about: Anchors S and E, a g path below them through X, and a link S to E pinned at P, passing the g anchor Y above.

older beside a younger route.about: An older link A-B on a g path through x above, and a younger link C-D on a middle g path through m1 and m2; A and B also reach the middle path, a longer way.

transit board.about: Two routers linked through a bare anchor by hand pipes, a lone router, and a host; no transit declared yet.

transit detour.about: The short way from A to B runs through a host, the long way over two bare anchors; no transit declared.

transit pin.about: A link from A to B pinned at P, over the pipes its w drag laid; no transit declared.

transit two pins.about: A link from A to B pinned at P then Q; no transit declared.

transit junction.about: Three links end at P, from A, B and C; no transit declared.

gestures.delete pin: Select an anchor a link is pinned at (a `w` anchor), and press Delete.
gestures.delete `g` hop: Select an anchor a link passes without pinning, and press Delete.
gestures.delete end: Select a link's end, a node or an anchor, and press Delete.
gestures.delete link: Select the link itself, and press Delete.
gestures.draw: mouseup on end: Drag from one end and release on the other, pressing nothing.
gestures.draw: `g` bend: Drag, press `g` at a point on the way, and release on the end.
gestures.draw: `g` on end: Drag to the end, press `g` on it, and release there.
gestures.draw: `w` bend: Drag, press `w` at a point on the way, and release on the end.
gestures.select link: Click a link to select it.
gestures.transit `x`: Select anchors or nodes, and press x.
gestures.draw: `w` on a non-transiting anchor: Turn an anchor's transit off, then drag a link, press w on that anchor, and release beyond it.
gestures.draw: `g` on a non-transiting anchor: Turn an anchor's transit off, then drag a link, press g on that anchor, and release beyond it.

rows.does: Select the centre anchor both links pass, and press Delete.
rows.intent: Both links stay, DOWN: dotted and straight between their ends. No pipe is created.

expect.notice: 2 links down

rows.rule: DECISIONS: "A down link is not a deleted link" (2026-09-29).

rows.does: Select the anchor the link is pinned at, and press Delete.
rows.intent: The pin goes, and the link with it: a pinned link lives and dies with its pins. The hand-laid way below, and its anchors, stay.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "A pinned link lives and dies with its pins" (2026-09-30), which reversed re-routing when a pin is deleted.

rows.does: Select the anchor the link is pinned at, and press Delete.
rows.intent: No other way exists, so the whole link is deleted; its pipes go and both nodes stay.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "A link that loses a pin with no other way is deleted whole" (2026-09-29).

rows.does: Select the middle pin, P2, and press Delete.
rows.intent: P1 to P3 has no pipe, so the whole link goes, with every w anchor and pipe it laid.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "A link that loses a pin with no other way is deleted whole" (2026-09-29).

rows.does: Select the first pin, P1, and press Delete.
rows.intent: The start has no other pipe, so the whole link goes, with every w anchor and pipe it laid.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "A link that loses a pin with no other way is deleted whole" (2026-09-29).

rows.does: Select the end anchor, E, and press Delete.
rows.intent: The link is gone with its end, permanently, and every w anchor and pipe it laid goes with it.
rows.rule: The director, 2026-09-29: "if either source or dest node is deleted, link is gone with it permanently". DECISIONS: "deliberate" means held by the pipes laid with g (2026-09-29).

rows.does: Select the start anchor, S, and press Delete.
rows.intent: The link is gone with its start, permanently, and every w anchor and pipe it laid goes with it.
rows.rule: The director, 2026-09-29: "if either source or dest node is deleted, link is gone with it permanently". DECISIONS: "deliberate" means held by the pipes laid with g (2026-09-29).

rows.does: Select the link on its first leg, and press Delete.
rows.intent: The link goes, with every w anchor and pipe it laid; its own dying pipes shelter nothing.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "deliberate" means held by the pipes laid with g (2026-09-29).

rows.does: Select the g anchor between the two pins, and press Delete.
rows.intent: No pin is lost, so the link stays, DOWN: dotted through both its pins, with the pipes on its intent kept for it to heal onto.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Three readings of the delete and drag rules, confirmed" (2026-09-30) -- "Stays, shown down".

rows.does: Select the left centre, which both left links pin, and press Delete.
rows.intent: Both pinned links have no other way and are deleted whole; the two links passing the right centre are untouched and up.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "A link that loses a pin with no other way is deleted whole" (2026-09-29).

rows.does: Select node B, the link's end, and press Delete.
rows.intent: The link is gone with its end, and nothing of it remains: its pin and its pipes go too.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Seed boards give each pipe the lifetime its gesture would" (2026-09-29).

rows.does: Select node B, and press Delete.
rows.intent: A-B is gone with its end; C-D still runs through the centre, and the centre and its hand pipes stay.
rows.rule: The director, 2026-09-29, on deleting an end. DECISIONS: pipes laid by hand stay until deleted (2026-09-27).

rows.does: Select the right centre, which the two right links only pass, and press Delete.
rows.intent: No pin is lost, so both right links stay, DOWN: dotted and straight between their ends. The pinned pair on the left is untouched.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "A down link is not a deleted link" (2026-09-29).

rows.does: Select the first pin, P1, and press Delete.
rows.intent: The start has no other way, so the whole link goes. The g anchor keeps its remaining hand pipe, and that pipe keeps P2.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "A pinned link lives and dies with its pins" and "Three readings of the delete and drag rules, confirmed" (2026-09-30) -- "P2 stays".

rows.does: Select node A, and press Delete.
rows.intent: A-B is gone with its end, permanently: a down link does not wait to heal once an end is deleted. C-D stays down.
rows.rule: The director, 2026-09-29: "if either source or dest node is deleted, link is gone with it permanently".

rows.does: Select link A-B on its left leg, and press Delete.
rows.intent: A-B goes. C-D still runs through the centre, which its hand pipes keep, and all four hand pipes stay.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: pipes laid by hand stay until deleted (2026-09-27).

rows.does: Select the centre anchor both links pass, and press Delete.
rows.intent: The down links are drawn ORANGE as well as dotted, so down reads apart from a live link at a glance.
rows.rule: The director, 2026-09-29: "we need to make the dots a different color - orange?". The shade is the proposer's: #ff9800, apart from the transit ring #ffb74d and the packet placeholder #ffa726.

rows.does: Drag from A, press g above the old centre, press g on B, and release.
rows.intent: g lays pipes and makes no link: the g anchor and its two hand pipes are laid, and the down A-B heals over them, drawn through the new anchor. The notice says the pipes were laid and that A-B healed.

expect.notice: 2 pipes laid.*link-000001 healed

rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Each drag action does one thing" (2026-09-30). The director's report on the g bend, 2026-09-29.

rows.does: Drag from A to B, press g on B, and release there.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Each drag action does one thing" (2026-09-30). The director asked, 2026-09-29, whether g on an existing anchor should differ from a plain mouseup: it does -- g lays a pipe, a mouseup makes a link.
rows.intent: g on the end lays the pipe from A to B by hand, and no link is made; the down A-B heals over it.

expect.notice: 1 pipe laid.*link-000001 healed

rows.does: Drag from A, and release on B.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: the reading under "Each drag action does one thing", CONFIRMED 2026-09-30 -- nothing is made, and the notice says why.
rows.intent: Nothing is made, and the notice says why: a plain drag lays no pipes, and A-B already has an unpinned link, which a pair takes one of.

expect.notice: already joins

rows.does: Drag from A, press w above the old centre, and release on B.
rows.intent: A new link, pinned at the new anchor, is made in addition to the down A-B, which stays down. w laid the pipe into its anchor and the release on B, after a key, laid the last one -- both with the new link and carrying only it -- so the new link is up.
rows.rule: The director, 2026-09-29: "w pins and draws an entirely new link in addition to the broken one". DECISIONS: "A release lays the final pipe whenever a key was pressed before it" (2026-09-30).

rows.does: Drag from A, press w above the old centre, release on B, then delete the new link.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "A w pipe goes when no link is on it or resolves onto it" (2026-09-30). The director accepted that this case leaves a trace ("Yes: nothing recorded"), amending "Draw-then-delete leaves no trace" (2026-09-25) for it.
rows.intent: A-B stays down while the w link exists, which has first call on its pipes. Deleting the w link frees them, and A-B, waiting on that way, takes them and heals: the w anchor and both pipes stay, now carrying A-B.

rows.does: Drag from A, and release on C.
rows.intent: A link from A to C is made and lays no pipes. The only way, through the centre, is held by the two links already there, so it is made down, and, selected as it is made, it says the two links hold its way.

expect.notice: link-\w+ is down: its way is held by link-000001, link-000002

rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Each drag action does one thing" (2026-09-30). DECISIONS: "Pipes carry one link each, for now" (2026-09-30).

rows.does: Drag from A, press w on t1, and release on B.
rows.intent: The new link is made, pinned at t1, but the pipe from A to t1 already carries the upper link, and a pipe carries one link: it is made down, and, selected as it is made, it says the upper link holds its way.

expect.notice: link-\w+ is down: its way is held by link-000001

rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Each drag action does one thing" (2026-09-30). DECISIONS: "Pipes carry one link each, for now" (2026-09-30).

rows.does: Click the lower link, which is down.
rows.intent: The lower link is selected, the upper link blocking its way is highlighted orange, and the notice says the lower link is down because the upper one holds its way.

expect.notice: link-000002 is down: its way is held by link-000001

rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Selecting a blocked link highlights the link blocking it" (2026-09-30).

rows.does: Select the upper link on the trunk, and press Delete.
rows.intent: The trunk is free, so the lower link heals and is drawn along it; the trunk's hand pipes stay.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Pipes carry one link each, for now" (2026-09-30). DECISIONS: a down link heals when a way returns (2026-09-25).

rows.does: Click the upper link, which is up.
rows.intent: Selecting a link that is up highlights nothing else: only a down link has blockers to show.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Selecting a blocked link highlights the link blocking it" (2026-09-30); the lower link is orange only because it is down (2026-09-29).

rows.does: Delete the upper link, select the lower one (now on the trunk), then undo with it still selected.
rows.intent: Undo restores the upper link with its age, so it takes the trunk back and the lower link is down again. The lower link is still selected, so the upper link is highlighted as its blocker at once.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Pipes carry one link each, for now" and "Selecting a blocked link highlights the link blocking it" (2026-09-30).

rows.does: Drag from A, press g off the existing way, press g on C, and release.
rows.intent: g lays pipes and makes no link: the g anchor and two hand pipes are laid, and the links already there are untouched.

expect.notice: 2 pipes laid

rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Each drag action does one thing" (2026-09-30).

rows.does: Drag from A, press g off the existing way, and release on C without a key.
rows.intent: The drag lays only pipes, so the release on C lays the last pipe into it: the g anchor and two hand pipes, and no link.

expect.notice: 2 pipes laid

rows.rule: DECISIONS: "In a drag that lays only pipes, a release on an anchor lays the last pipe into it" (2026-09-30).

rows.does: Drag from S, and release on E.
rows.intent: A link is made and lays no pipes: it runs the shorter path, the four pipes above, and the path below is its alternate.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Each drag action does one thing" (2026-09-30). DECISIONS: "A g drag with a shorter free way makes the link on that way" (2026-09-30), for the director's alternate-path case.

rows.does: Make the link as in ALT-01, then delete the middle anchor of the path above.
rows.intent: The link moves onto the path below and stays up: that is what the alternate is for.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Each drag action does one thing" (2026-09-30). DECISIONS: a link routes on by the fewest pipes when its way breaks (2026-09-26).

rows.does: Click C-B, which is down.
rows.intent: C-B is blocked, not wayless: its way runs over A-B's w pipes, which A-B has first call on. The notice says A-B holds its way.

expect.notice: is down: its way is held by link-

rows.rule: DECISIONS: "A w pipe goes when no link is on it or resolves onto it" (2026-09-30).

rows.does: Select A-B on its first leg, and press Delete.
rows.intent: C-B takes over the freed w path and comes up, drawn through P1 and P2. The pipes it runs over, and P2, stay; A's lone pipe, which no link is on, goes with A.
rows.rule: The director's report, 2026-09-30: "If I delete link A-B - I would expect C-B to route over the top of the now-free path". DECISIONS: "A w pipe goes when no link is on it or resolves onto it" (2026-09-30).

rows.state: two pins beside a g path
rows.does: Select Q, the second pin, and press Delete.
rows.intent: The link loses Q, and the only way left from P to E runs back over S-P and round the g path below: a hairpin, which is no way. So it has no other way and is deleted whole, with P and its w pipes; the g path stays.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "A link never runs the same pipe twice" (2026-09-30). DECISIONS: "A link that loses a pin with no other way is deleted whole" (2026-09-29).

rows.state: a pin and a g hop beside a g path
rows.does: Select Y, the g anchor the link passes, and press Delete.
rows.intent: No pin is lost, and the only way left from P to E would double back over S-P: no way, so the link is down, drawn dotted through its pin P.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "A link never runs the same pipe twice" (2026-09-30).

rows.does: Delete x, the g anchor the older link A-B passes, then click the younger link C-D.
rows.intent: A-B loses its way and, being older, takes the middle path C-D is routed over; C-D is down, and says A-B holds its way.

expect.notice: is down: its way is held by link-

rows.rule: DECISIONS: "An older link may supplant a younger link's route" (2026-09-30).

rows.does: Press w below to place S, then drag from S to the pin P1, and release.
rows.intent: S is still the sole selected anchor and the next gesture drags from it, so the w that placed it is the drag's first key: a link from S to P1 with its pipe, up. P1 becomes a junction, cutting the chain there.
rows.rule: The director's report, 2026-09-30: "it becomes a junction (correctly). However it didnt lay the pipes". DECISIONS: "The w that placed the source counts as the drag's first key" (2026-09-30).

rows.does: Press w below to place S, click away, then drag from S to P1, and release.
rows.intent: The click away clears the w, so the drag follows the normal rules: a plain link that lays no pipe, made down; the junction is still made.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "The w that placed the source counts as the drag's first key" (2026-09-30). "This eliminates the case where you click off the anchor to unselect it".

rows.does: Press w below to place S, then drag from S with g at a point and g on the end E, and release.
rows.intent: A g in the drag cancels the source w: two hand pipes are laid and no link is made, so the chain is untouched.

expect.notice: 2 pipes laid

rows.rule: DECISIONS: "The w that placed the source counts as the drag's first key" (2026-09-30). Asked whether a g in the drag cancels it, the director chose "A g in the drag cancels it".

rows.does: Drag from A, press w on node C, and release there.
rows.intent: A direct link from A to C, with its pipe laid with it, and up: w may be pressed on a node as the last hop.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "w may be pressed on a node as the last hop" (2026-09-30).

rows.does: Draw the pinned link again: drag from A, press w on its pin, press w on B, and release.
rows.intent: The planner refuses a second link on the same pair bending at the same anchor. The notice says so, and the tab shows nothing of the refused link: it holds exactly what the planner holds.
rows.rule: Production resynchronises a tab whose optimistic change the server refused (app/src/sync.js, requestResync); the lab mounts the same rule (B260).

rows.does: Delete the middle pin, then undo.
rows.intent: One undo restores the link with its three pins and all five anchors. Its pipes are not restored, being session state until the format batch (F6), so it returns down.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "A link that loses a pin with no other way is deleted whole" (2026-09-29), as CORRECTED for undo.

rows.does: Select the bare anchor, and press x.
rows.intent: The anchor's transit goes off and the ring shows it: thin, dashed, light orange. What that does to the link through it is TRN-06's (stage X2).

expect.notice: transit off at w5

rows.rule: DECISIONS: "The transit gesture" and "The transit mark" (2026-09-28); "Transit with pipes" (2026-09-30), TR-6 and TR-7.

rows.does: Select the bare anchor, and press x twice.
rows.intent: Two states: the second press turns transit back on, and the ring goes.

expect.notice: transit on

rows.rule: DECISIONS: "The transit gesture" and "The transit mark" (2026-09-28); "Transit with pipes" (2026-09-30), TR-6 and TR-7.

rows.does: Select the lone router, and press x.
rows.intent: A router offers the choice, so its transit goes off and it shows the ring, drawn as on an anchor.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "The transit gesture" and "The transit mark" (2026-09-28); "Transit with pipes" (2026-09-30), TR-6 and TR-7.

rows.does: Select the host, and press x.
rows.intent: A host offers no choice -- its transit is always off -- so nothing is declared, no ring is drawn, and the notice says why.

expect.notice: host.*never passes

rows.rule: DECISIONS: "The transit gesture" and "The transit mark" (2026-09-28); "Transit with pipes" (2026-09-30), TR-6 and TR-7.

rows.does: Turn the anchor's transit off; then select the anchor and the lone router together, and press x.
rows.intent: Each selected anchor is flipped on its own: the anchor comes back on and the router goes off, rather than both being driven to one value.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "The transit gesture" and "The transit mark" (2026-09-28); "Transit with pipes" (2026-09-30), TR-6 and TR-7.

rows.does: Select the bare anchor the link runs through, and press x.
rows.intent: No route may pass a non-transiting anchor, and the link has no other way: it goes down, its pipes kept for it to heal onto, and the notice counts it.

expect.notice: transit off at w5 -- 1 link down

rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Transit with pipes" (2026-09-30), TR-1, TR-4 and TR-6.

rows.does: Select the bare anchor, and press x twice.
rows.intent: Turning transit back on heals the link over the same pipes.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Transit with pipes" (2026-09-30), TR-1, TR-4 and TR-6.

rows.does: Turn the bare anchor's transit off, then click the link, which is down.
rows.intent: A selected down link says why: its way passes an anchor whose transit is off, and it heals when transit is turned back on.

rows.does: Select the host on the short way, and press x.

rows.does: Select the first anchor on the long way, and press x.
rows.intent: With the host blocking the short way and the anchor the long way, the link has no way left and goes down.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Transit with pipes" (2026-09-30), TR-1, TR-4 and TR-6.

rows.intent: Turned back on, the link heals the long way -- never through the host.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Transit with pipes" (2026-09-30), TR-1, TR-4 and TR-6.

rows.does: Select the pin P, and press x.
rows.intent: A link cannot bend where what arrives stops: it is cut at P into two links that both end there, each up over its own pipe, and the pipes stay.

expect.notice: transit off at P -- 1 link cut in two there

rows.does: Turn P's transit off, then select the link from C and press Delete.
rows.intent: Two links are left ending at P, and P's transit is off, so they stay two: what arrives at P stops there.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Transit with pipes" (2026-09-30), TR-5; "Two separately drawn links left alone at a point join into one" (2026-09-26).

rows.does: Select the link from C and press Delete, transit untouched.
rows.intent: With transit on, the two links left alone at P join into one, as ruled -- the comparison TRN-19 departs from.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "Transit with pipes" (2026-09-30), TR-5; "Two separately drawn links left alone at a point join into one" (2026-09-26).

rows.does: Select P, where three links end, and press x.
rows.intent: What arrives at P stops there, so P is an endpoint for each of the three links -- drawn with the endpoint ring and the transit ring, never a junction -- and the links stay three.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "A non-transiting anchor has endpoints only, under one ring" (2026-10-02), B277; TRANSIT.md section 4.

rows.does: Select P, where three links end, and press x twice.
rows.intent: Turned back on, the three links meet at P again: a junction, with no transit ring -- the comparison TRN-21 departs from.
rows.rule: DECISIONS: "A non-transiting anchor has endpoints only, under one ring" (2026-10-02), B277; TRANSIT.md section 4.
